statements.impact_statement: rustls-webpki 0.102 compares only the first CRL distribution point of a certificate when it checks revocation, so a revoked certificate can pass when unknown revocation status is allowed. The broker never runs that check. rumqttc 0.25.1, the only crate linking rustls-webpki 0.102, names it only as the type of an error variant that nothing constructs and calls none of its functions, and the broker verifies every certificate with rustls-webpki 0.103.17, which is patched, and with no revocation lists.

rustls-webpki 0.102 ignores name constraints on URI names when it verifies a certificate path, so a misissued certificate can pass a constraint it breaks. The broker never runs that verification. rumqttc 0.25.1, the only crate linking rustls-webpki 0.102, names it only as the type of an error variant that nothing constructs and calls none of its functions, and the broker verifies every certificate with rustls-webpki 0.103.17, which rejects URI name constraints.

rustls-webpki 0.102 accepts a certificate for a wildcard DNS name under a permitted name constraint the wildcard reaches past when it verifies a certificate path. The broker never runs that verification. rumqttc 0.25.1, the only crate linking rustls-webpki 0.102, names it only as the type of an error variant that nothing constructs and calls none of its functions, and the broker verifies every certificate with rustls-webpki 0.103.17, which is patched.

rustls-webpki 0.102 panics when it parses a certificate revocation list whose issuing distribution point holds an empty onlySomeReasons bit string. The broker parses no revocation lists. rumqttc 0.25.1, the only crate linking rustls-webpki 0.102, names it only as the type of an error variant that nothing constructs and calls none of its functions, and the broker's certificate checks run on rustls-webpki 0.103.17, which is patched, with no revocation lists.

rustls-webpki 0.102 accepts certificate paths through the distrusted emSign intermediates, whose private keys are public, when its trust anchors lead to them. The broker never verifies a path with it. rumqttc 0.25.1, the only crate linking rustls-webpki 0.102, names it only as the type of an error variant that nothing constructs and calls none of its functions, and the broker verifies every certificate with rustls-webpki 0.103.17, which rejects those intermediates.
